<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Apply request-tracing documentation to open-api.json

```bash
cd "D:\Documents\Learning\InterviewProjects\DockSlot" && node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const spec = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('open-api.json', 'utf8'));

// --- 1. Reusable parameter: the correlation id clients may supply -------------
spec.components.parameters = {
    RequestIdHeader: {
        in: 'header',
        name: 'X-Request-ID',
        required: false,
        schema: { type: 'string', maxLength: 128, pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._:+-]+\$' },
        description:
            'Correlation id for this request. Supply your own to join DockSlot logs with your ' +
            'application logs, or omit it and the server will generate a UUID. Values that are ' +
            'longer than 128 characters or contain characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._:+-] are ' +
            'rejected and replaced by a generated UUID. The value (supplied or generated) is ' +
            'echoed back on the X-Request-ID response header, written to the booking outbox ' +
            'payload, and logged by the background delivery worker.',
        example: '7f8a1b2c-3d4e-5f6a-7b8c-9d0e1f2a3b4c'
    }
};

// --- 2. Reusable response header ---------------------------------------------
spec.components.headers = {
    RequestId: {
        description:
            'The correlation id for this request: the value you sent on the X-Request-ID request ' +
            'header, or a server-generated UUID. Present on every response, including errors. ' +
            'Quote it when reporting an issue so the full request trace can be retrieved.',
        schema: { type: 'string', maxLength: 128 },
        example: '7f8a1b2c-3d4e-5f6a-7b8c-9d0e1f2a3b4c'
    }
};

// --- 3. Document the tracing contract globally --------------------------------
spec.info.description = [
    'API documentation for multi-tenant logistics platform.',
    '',
    '## End-to-end request tracing',
    '',
    'Every response carries an X-Request-ID header. Send that header on the request to correlate ' +
        'a call with your own logs; omit it and the server generates a UUID.',
    '',
    'The id is recorded on the structured log line of the HTTP request and its response, ' +
        'persisted inside the booking outbox payload, and included in every log line the ' +
        'background delivery worker emits. Booking endpoints therefore hand back a single id that ' +
        'follows a booking from the API call, through the MySQL outbox row, to the carrier ' +
        'webhook delivery - including each retry attempt.'
].join('\n');

// --- 4. Reference the parameter/header on the traced booking mutations --------
// These are the operations that persist a request id into an outbox payload.
const traced = [
    ['/bookings', 'post', '201'],
    ['/bookings/{id}/reschedule', 'patch', '200'],
    ['/bookings/{id}/reschedule', 'put', '200'],
    ['/bookings/{id}/cancel', 'patch', '200'],
    ['/bookings/{id}', 'delete', '200'],
    ['/bookings/{id}/status', 'patch', '200']
];

let touched = 0;
for (const [path, method, successStatus] of traced) {
    const op = spec.paths[path] && spec.paths[path][method];
    if (!op) {
        console.warn('MISSING operation: ' + method.toUpperCase() + ' ' + path);
        continue;
    }

    op.parameters = op.parameters || [];
    const alreadyReferenced = op.parameters.some((p) => p && p.\$ref === '#/components/parameters/RequestIdHeader');
    if (!alreadyReferenced) {
        op.parameters.push({ \$ref: '#/components/parameters/RequestIdHeader' });
    }

    const response = op.responses && op.responses[successStatus];
    if (response) {
        response.headers = response.headers || {};
        response.headers['X-Request-ID'] = { \$ref: '#/components/headers/RequestId' };
    } else {
        console.warn('MISSING response ' + successStatus + ' on ' + method.toUpperCase() + ' ' + path);
    }
    touched++;
}

fs.writeFileSync('open-api.json', JSON.stringify(spec, null, 4) + '\n');
console.log('updated ' + touched + ' operation(s)');
"
```

End-to-end request tracing is implemented and verified.

## What changed

**1. Request ID middleware + structured logger**

- `backend/src/utils/requestContext.ts` *(new)* — `AsyncLocalStorage` carrying `{ requestId }`. This is what lets `booking.service.ts` read the id without threading `req` through every service signature.
- `backend/src/utils/logger.ts` — converted the dead `console`-based stub into a Pino logger. Pretty output in dev, raw NDJSON in prod/test (the pretty transport spawns a worker thread that would hang vitest), plus redaction of `authorization`/`cookie`/`[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]`/`token` paths and a `childLogger()` helper that drops `undefined` bindings.
- `backend/src/middleware/requestLogger.ts` *(new)* — reads `X-Request-ID`, else `uuidv4()`; attaches `req.requestId`, echoes it on the response, logs the request/response pair with method, url, status, duration, user, and runs the rest of the request inside the ALS scope.
- `backend/src/app.ts` — mounted **first**, ahead of CORS and the rate limiter, so even rejected requests get a correlation id.
- `backend/src/middleware/logging.middleware.ts` — its stub `requestLogger` was dead code and shadowed the new one; it's now a re-export so only one implementation exists.

Two things I decided rather than asked:
- **Header sanitisation.** An unsanitised inbound `X-Request-ID` is a log-forging and response-header-injection vector, so anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:+-]` or over 128 chars is discarded for a server-generated UUID.
- **Installed `pino`, `uuid` (+`pino-pretty`, `@types/uuid` as dev)** — none were present. `uuid` was installed specifically because you asked for `uuidv4()`; note the codebase already used `randomUUID` from `crypto` elsewhere.

**2. Outbox payload propagation** — `requestId` added to `EnqueueOutboxInput`/`OutboxPayload` and the persisted JSON; `booking.service.ts` [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es `getRequestId()` at all four transactional enqueue sites (create, reschedule, cancel, status change). `enqueue` also falls back to the ambient context, so a future call site can't silently lose tracing.

**3. Worker trace logging** — `outbox.worker.ts` now uses a per-event child logger binding `eventId`, `bookingId`, and `requestId`, on claim, dispatch, success, non-retryable park, and backoff-retry lines. Legacy rows without a `requestId` log cleanly without the field.

**4. `open-api.json`** — added reusable `components.parameters.RequestIdHeader` and `components.headers.RequestId`, referenced on the six booking-mutation operations that write an outbox event, and documented the contract in `info.description`.

## Verification

Typecheck is clean (`tsc --noEmit`). I verified behaviour with temporary harnesses against the real MySQL, then deleted them:

- 16 checks on header trust/sanitisation, payload construction, and — the assumption I most wanted to prove — that ALS survives `prisma.$transaction`: a real `createBooking` inside a request scope persisted the exact id into the outbox JSON (and omitted it when there was no scope).
- The app boots with the default pretty logger; responses echo `X-Request-ID`; every request and response log line carries it (one response line per request — the abort guard doesn't double-log).
- Worker claim/dispatch/success/backoff lines all emit the `requestId`/`eventId`/`bookingId` triple, using a stubbed outbox service so no existing rows were touched.

I also added a regression test to the existing `scratch_test_outbox.ts` (TEST 11: id reaches the webhook body) in that file's own style. **I could not run it** — Redis is down on this machine and it needs the mock carrier, so that test is typechecked but unexecuted; its assertions mirror behaviour I verified individually.

Two notes: `redis` is not running locally (so authenticated HTTP flows fail here), and `open-api.json` has pre-existing drift from the router — it documents a `DELETE /bookings/{id}` that doesn't exist and omits `PATCH /bookings/{id}`. I left both alone as out of scope.

Implementation of the timeout:

```ts
function withTimeout<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`Database health check timed out after ${ms}ms`)), ms);
    timer.unref?.();
    promise.then(
      (v) => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(v); },
      (e) => { clearTimeout(timer); reject(e); }
    );
  });
}
```

Implementation:

```ts
import { prisma } from './config/db.config';
import { childLogger } from './utils/logger';

/**
 * Upper bound on the liveness/readiness probe's database round-trip. A probe
 * that hangs is worse than one that fails: the container runtime would wait for
 * its own deadline instead of getting a fast 503 and rescheduling.
 */
const HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = (() => {
  const parsed = parseInt(process.env.HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS || '', 10);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : 3000;
})();

function withTimeout<T>(promise: Promise<T>, timeoutMs: number): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(
      () => reject(new Error(`Database health check timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`)),
      timeoutMs
    );
    timer.unref?.();

    promise.then(
      (value) => {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        resolve(value);
      },
      (error) => {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        reject(error);
      }
    );
  });
}
```

Handler:

```ts
/**
 * GET /health
 * Public readiness probe. Verifies the service can actually serve traffic by
 * round-tripping a trivial query to MySQL through Prisma.
 *
 * 200 UP   - process is running and the database answers.
 * 503 DOWN - the database is unreachable or the probe timed out.
 *
 * Deliberately unauthenticated and outside /api: orchestrators (Kubernetes,
 * ECS, Docker healthcheck) must reach it before auth infra is ready.
 */
const healthCheck = async (req: Request, res: Response): Promise<void> => {
  // Probes must never be served from a proxy or CDN cache.
  res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-store');
  const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();

  try {
    await withTimeout(prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1`, HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS);

    res.status(200).json({
      status: 'UP',
      database: 'connected',
      timestamp,
    });
  } catch (error: any) {
    childLogger({ requestId: req.requestId }).error(
      { err: error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)) },
      'Health check failed: database is not reachable.'
    );

    res.status(503).json({
      status: 'DOWN',
      database: 'disconnected',
      error: error?.message || String(error),
      timestamp,
    });
  }
};

app.get('/health', healthCheck);
```

```typescript
import { prisma } from '../config/db.config';
import { childLogger } from '../utils/logger';
import { getRequestId } from '../utils/requestContext';

/**
 * HealthService
 * -------------
 * Infrastructure-level health checks. This layer owns *how* the service is
 * probed (which dependency, with what timeout) but knows nothing about HTTP -
 * it returns a plain result, and the controller decides the status code.
 *
 * Kept free of Express types so the same check can be reused from a boot-time
 * self-check, a smoke-test script, or a future CLI without pulling in HTTP.
 */

export type HealthStatus = 'UP' | 'DOWN';
export type DatabaseStatus = 'connected' | 'disconnected';

export interface HealthCheckResult {
  status: HealthStatus;
  database: DatabaseStatus;
  /** ISO 8601 timestamp of when the probe completed. */
  timestamp: string;
  /** Present only when the check failed. */
  error?: string;
}

const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000;

/**
 * Upper bound on the probe's database round-trip. A probe that hangs is worse
 * than one that fails: the orchestrator would wait for its own deadline instead
 * of receiving a fast 503 and rescheduling the container.
 */
function readTimeoutMs(): number {
  const parsed = parseInt(process.env.HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS || '', 10);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
}

export class HealthService {
  public readonly timeoutMs: number;

  constructor(timeoutMs: number = readTimeoutMs()) {
    this.timeoutMs = timeoutMs;
  }

  /**
   * Probes MySQL through Prisma with a trivial query.
   *
   * Never throws: every failure - unreachable server, auth error, or timeout -
   * is converted into a `DOWN` result so a probe can always answer. Failures are
   * logged with the request's correlation id so an unhealthy reading in the logs
   * can be tied back to the orchestrator's probe request.
   */
  public async check(): Promise<HealthCheckResult> {
    const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();

    try {
      await this.withTimeout(prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1`, this.timeoutMs);

      return {
        status: 'UP',
        database: 'connected',
        timestamp,
      };
    } catch (error) {
      const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));

      childLogger({ requestId: getRequestId() }).error(
        { err, timeoutMs: this.timeoutMs },
        'Health check failed: the database is not reachable.'
      );

      return {
        status: 'DOWN',
        database: 'disconnected',
        error: err.message,
        timestamp,
      };
    }
  }

  /**
   * Rejects if `promise` has not settled within `timeoutMs`. The timer is
   * unref'd so a pending probe can never hold the event loop open.
   */
  private withTimeout<T>(promise: Promise<T>, timeoutMs: number): Promise<T> {
    return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
      const timer = setTimeout(
        () => reject(new Error(`Database health check timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`)),
        timeoutMs
      );
      timer.unref?.();

      promise.then(
        (value) => {
          clearTimeout(timer);
          resolve(value);
        },
        (error) => {
          clearTimeout(timer);
          reject(error);
        }
      );
    });
  }
}

export const healthService = new HealthService();

```

```typescript
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { healthService } from '../services/health.service';

/**
 * GET /health - readiness/liveness probe.
 *
 * Maps the service-level health result onto HTTP:
 *   200 UP   - the process is running and the database answers.
 *   503 DOWN - the database is unreachable, errored, or the probe timed out.
 *
 * The heavy lifting (dependency selection, timeout policy, failure logging)
 * lives in `healthService`; this handler only owns HTTP concerns.
 */
export const healthCheck = async (_req: Request, res: Response): Promise<void> => {
  // Health responses describe a single instant; never let a proxy or CDN cache them.
  res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-store');

  // `check()` is guaranteed not to throw, so there is nothing to catch here.
  const result = await healthService.check();

  res.status(result.status === 'UP' ? 200 : 503).json(result);
};

```

```text
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "mysql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum OrganizationType {
  WAREHOUSE_OPERATOR
  CARRIER
}

enum UserRole {
  WAREHOUSE_ADMIN
  DOCK_MANAGER
  CARRIER_ADMIN
  DISPATCHER
}

enum DockStatus {
  ACTIVE
  MAINTENANCE
}

enum BookingStatus {
  BOOKED
  CANCELLED
  ARRIVED
  NO_SHOW
  COMPLETED
}

model Organization {
  id        Int              @id @default(autoincrement())
  name      String
  type      OrganizationType
  createdAt DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime         @updatedAt

  users       User[]
  warehouses  Warehouse[]
  bookings    Booking[]    @relation("CarrierBookings")
  invitations Invitation[]

  @@map("organizations")
}

model User {
  id                   Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  organizationId       Int
  email                String    @unique
  [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]Hash         String
  role                 UserRole
  isActive             Boolean   @default(true)
  isEmailVerified      Boolean   @default(false)
  verificationToken    String?   @unique
  resetPasswordToken   String?   @unique
  resetPasswordExpires DateTime?
  failedLoginAttempts  Int       @default(0)
  lockUntil            DateTime?
  totpSecret           String?
  isTwoFactorEnabled   Boolean   @default(false)
  createdAt            DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt            DateTime  @updatedAt

  organization Organization @relation(fields: [organizationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  auditLogs    AuditLog[]

  @@index([organizationId])
  @@map("users")
}

model Warehouse {
  id                Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  organizationId    Int
  name              String
  address           String
  timezone          String
  slotLengthMinutes Int      @default(30)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  organization   Organization     @relation(fields: [organizationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  docks          Dock[]
  operatingHours OperatingHour[]
  policy         WarehousePolicy?

  @@index([organizationId])
  @@map("warehouses")
}

model Dock {
  id          Int        @id @default(autoincrement())
  warehouseId Int
  name        String
  status      DockStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  createdAt   DateTime   @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime   @updatedAt

  warehouse Warehouse     @relation(fields: [warehouseId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  bookings  Booking[]
  closures  DockClosure[]

  @@index([warehouseId])
  @@map("docks")
}

model DockClosure {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  dockId    Int
  startTime DateTime
  endTime   DateTime
  reason    String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  dock      Dock     @relation(fields: [dockId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([dockId])
  @@index([dockId, startTime, endTime], map: "dock_closures_active_check_idx")
  @@map("dock_closures")
}

model OperatingHour {
  id                Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  warehouseId       Int
  dayOfWeek         Int
  openTime          String
  closeTime         String
  slotLengthMinutes Int
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  warehouse Warehouse @relation(fields: [warehouseId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([warehouseId])
  @@map("operating_hours")
}

model Booking {
  id            Int           @id @default(autoincrement())
  dockId        Int
  carrierOrgId  Int
  slotStartTime DateTime
  slotEndTime   DateTime
  truckPlate    String?
  driverName    String?
  driverPhone   String?
  cargoNote     String?       @db.Text
  status        BookingStatus @default(BOOKED)
  activeLock    String?       @default("ACTIVE") @db.VarChar(50)
  createdAt     DateTime      @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime      @updatedAt

  dock       Dock         @relation(fields: [dockId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  carrierOrg Organization @relation("CarrierBookings", fields: [carrierOrgId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  auditLogs  AuditLog[]

  @@unique([dockId, slotStartTime, activeLock])
  @@index([dockId])
  @@index([carrierOrgId])
  @@map("bookings")
}

model AuditLog {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  bookingId Int
  userId    Int
  action    String   // "CREATED", "RESCHEDULED", "CANCELLED", "STATUS_CHANGED"
  details   Json?    // Stores old vs new values, reason, etc.
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  booking   Booking  @relation(fields: [bookingId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([bookingId])
  @@index([userId])
  @@map("audit_logs")
}

/// Transactional Outbox: events are written in the same transaction as the
/// aggregate mutation, then dispatched to the carrier webhook by a background
/// polling worker with exponential backoff.
model OutboxEvent {
  id            Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  eventId       String   @unique @default(uuid()) // stable idempotency key sent as X-Event-Id to the receiver
  aggregateType String   // e.g., "BOOKING"
  aggregateId   Int      // Booking ID
  payload       Json     // Full event details (carrier org, booking info, message)
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  retryCount    Int      @default(0)
  maxRetries    Int      @default(5)
  nextRetryAt   DateTime @default(now())
  lastError     String?  @db.Text // populated on failure for administrative review
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([status, nextRetryAt])
  @@index([aggregateType, aggregateId])
```

```text
1	import { Request } from 'express';
2	import rateLimit, { ipKeyGenerator } from 'express-rate-limit';
3	import { RedisStore } from 'rate-limit-redis';
4	import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
5	import redis from '../config/redis';
6	import { securityConfig } from '../config/security.config';
7	
8	/**
9	 * Dynamic RedisStore that always reads the current `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`
10	 * from `securityConfig` on each increment operation.
11	 */
12	class ConfigurableRedisStore extends RedisStore {
13	  override async increment(key: string) {
14	    this.windowMs = securityConfig.rateLimitWindowMs;
15	    return super.increment(key);
16	  }
17	}
18	
19	/**
20	 * Extracts user identifier from authenticated request (`req.user`) or Bearer token,
21	 * falling back to normalized client IP address (`ipKeyGenerator`).
22	 */
23	function resolveRateLimitKey(req: Request): string {
24	  if (req.user?.userId) {
25	    return `user:${req.user.userId}`;
26	  }
27	
28	  const authHeader = req.headers.authorization;
29	  if (authHeader && authHeader.startsWith('Bearer ')) {
30	    const token = authHeader.split(' ')[1];
31	    try {
32	      const decoded = jwt.decode(token) as { userId?: number; id?: number } | null;
33	      const uid = decoded?.userId ?? decoded?.id;
34	      if (uid) {
35	        return `user:${uid}`;
36	      }
37	    } catch {
38	      // Ignore malformed token and fall back to IP
39	    }
40	  }
41	
42	  const rawIp = req.ip || req.socket?.remoteAddress || '127.0.0.1';
43	  return `ip:${ipKeyGenerator(rawIp)}`;
44	}
45	
46	/**
47	 * Global API Rate Limiter:
48	 * Restricts general API requests per user/IP to `RATE_LIMIT_API_MAX`
49	 * within the `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` window using RedisStore.
50	 */
51	export const apiRateLimiter = rateLimit({
52	  windowMs: securityConfig.rateLimitWindowMs,
53	  limit: () => securityConfig.rateLimitApiMax,
54	  standardHeaders: true,
55	  legacyHeaders: true,
56	  statusCode: 429,
57	  keyGenerator: (req: Request) => resolveRateLimitKey(req),
58	  store: new ConfigurableRedisStore({
59	    sendCommand: (...args: string[]) => redis.call(...args),
60	    prefix: 'rl:api:',
61	  }),
62	  validate: false,
63	  message: {
64	    success: false,
65	    message: 'Too many API requests. Please try again later.',
66	  },
67	});
68	
69	export const globalRateLimiter = apiRateLimiter;
70	
71	/**
72	 * Booking Rate Limiter:
73	 * Restricts booking creation (`POST /api/bookings`) to `RATE_LIMIT_BOOKING_MAX`
74	 * per user within the `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` window using RedisStore.
75	 */
76	export const bookingRateLimiter = rateLimit({
77	  windowMs: securityConfig.rateLimitWindowMs,
78	  limit: () => securityConfig.rateLimitBookingMax,
79	  standardHeaders: true,
80	  legacyHeaders: true,
81	  statusCode: 429,
82	  keyGenerator: (req: Request) => resolveRateLimitKey(req),
83	  store: new ConfigurableRedisStore({
84	    sendCommand: (...args: string[]) => redis.call(...args),
85	    prefix: 'rl:booking:',
86	  }),
87	  validate: false,
88	  message: {
89	    success: false,
90	    message: 'Too many booking requests. Please wait before creating more bookings.',
91	  },
92	});
93	
94	/**
95	 * Authentication Rate Limiter (backward-compatible export backed by RedisStore and securityConfig).
96	 */
97	export const authRateLimiter = rateLimit({
98	  windowMs: securityConfig.rateLimitWindowMs,
99	  limit: () => securityConfig.rateLimitApiMax,
100	  standardHeaders: true,
101	  legacyHeaders: true,
102	  statusCode: 429,
103	  keyGenerator: (req: Request) => {
104	    const rawIp = req.ip || req.socket?.remoteAddress || '127.0.0.1';
105	    return `ip:${ipKeyGenerator(rawIp)}`;
106	  },
107	  store: new ConfigurableRedisStore({
108	    sendCommand: (...args: string[]) => redis.call(...args),
109	    prefix: 'rl:auth:',
110	  }),
111	  validate: false,
112	  message: {
113	    success: false,
114	    message: 'Too many authentication attempts from this IP address. Please try again later.',
115	  },
116	});
117	
118	/**
119	 * Two-Factor Authentication Rate Limiter:
120	 * Throttles TOTP code submission to `RATE_LIMIT_2FA_MAX` per IP within the
121	 * `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` window.
122	 *
123	 * Without this, a 6-digit code (10^6 combinations) spread across the ~10 code
124	 * windows covered by a 5-minute temp token would be brute-forceable. The key is
125	 * IP-based because the temp token itself is not yet an authenticated principal,
126	 * and is scoped per endpoint so throttling one route does not lock the others.
127	 */
128	export const twoFactorRateLimiter = rateLimit({
129	  windowMs: securityConfig.rateLimitWindowMs,
130	  limit: () => securityConfig.rateLimit2faMax,
131	  standardHeaders: true,
132	  legacyHeaders: true,
133	  statusCode: 429,
134	  keyGenerator: (req: Request) => {
135	    const rawIp = req.ip || req.socket?.remoteAddress || '127.0.0.1';
136	    // req.route is not populated before the handler runs, so use the raw path.
137	    const route = (req.originalUrl || req.url || '').split('?')[0];
138	    return `2fa:${route}:ip:${ipKeyGenerator(rawIp)}`;
139	  },
140	  store: new ConfigurableRedisStore({
141	    sendCommand: (...args: string[]) => redis.call(...args),
142	    prefix: 'rl:2fa:',
143	  }),
144	  validate: false,
145	  message: {
146	    success: false,
147	    message:
148	      'Too many two-factor authentication attempts. Please wait a moment before trying again.',
149	  },
```

```text
53	OUTBOX_BACKOFF_BASE_MS=1000
54	OUTBOX_MAX_BACKOFF_MS=300000
55	# A PROCESSING event older than this is assumed orphaned and requeued (ms)
```

```text
src/test/scratch_test_outbox.ts:33:const { prisma } = require('../config/db.config');
---index.ts---
import type { Server } from 'http';
import app from './app';
import { prisma } from './config/db.config';
import { outboxWorker } from './workers/outbox.worker';

const PORT = process.env.PORT || 5000;

/** How long to wait for in-flight work before forcing the process to exit. */
const SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000;

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test') {
  const server: Server = app.listen(PORT, () => {
    console.log(`Server is running on port ${PORT}`);
    console.log(`Swagger documentation available at http://localhost:${PORT}/api-docs`);
  });

  // Start the transactional outbox drain loop. It runs entirely outside the
  // request path, so booking endpoints return as soon as the DB transaction commits.
  outboxWorker.start();

  let shuttingDown = false;

  const shutdown = async (signal: string) => {
    if (shuttingDown) return;
    shuttingDown = true;

    console.log(`[Server] ${signal} received. Shutting down gracefully...`);

    // Hard deadline: never hang the process on a stuck socket or delivery cycle.
    const forceExit = setTimeout(() => {
      console.error('[Server] Graceful shutdown timed out. Forcing exit.');
      process.exit(1);
    }, SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS);
    forceExit.unref();

    try {
      // 1. Stop dispatching and let any in-flight webhook cycle settle so no
      //    event is left stranded in PROCESSING.
      await outboxWorker.stop();

      // 2. Stop accepting new connections and finish in-flight HTTP responses.
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve()));

      // 3. Release database connections.
      await prisma.$disconnect();

      clearTimeout(forceExit);
      console.log('[Server] Shutdown complete.');
      process.exit(0);
    } catch (error: any) {
      console.error(`[Server] Error during shutdown: ${error?.message || String(error)}`);
      process.exit(1);
    }
  };

  process.on('SIGINT', () => void shutdown('SIGINT'));
  process.on('SIGTERM', () => void shutdown('SIGTERM'));
}

export { app };
export default app;
```

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DockSlot backend image
#
# One image serves both the API (port 5000) and the mock carrier (port 4001);
# docker-compose runs it with different commands. The [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] is multi-stage so
# the Alpine toolchain needed to compile native modules (bcrypt) and the npm
# cache never reach the final image.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

FROM node:18-alpine AS [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
WORKDIR /app

# Prisma needs OpenSSL on Alpine. python3/make/g++ are required only if bcrypt
# has no musl pre[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] and falls back to compiling from source.
RUN apk add --no-cache openssl libc6-compat python3 make g++

COPY backend/package.json backend/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY backend/tsconfig.json ./
COPY backend/prisma ./prisma
COPY backend/src ./src

# `prisma generate` is platform-specific: generating inside the Alpine image
# produces the musl query engine the container will load at runtime. The
# datasource URL is never connected during generate, so a placeholder is fine.
ENV DATABASE_URL="mysql://[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@localhost:3306/[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]"
RUN npx prisma generate

RUN npm run [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]

# ---
FROM node:18-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Prisma's query engine links against OpenSSL; libc6-compat keeps native addons
# (bcrypt) working on musl.
RUN apk add --no-cache openssl libc6-compat

ENV NODE_ENV=production

# Keep dev dependencies: the compose command runs `prisma db push`, `prisma db
# seed` (which invokes ts-node), and the mock carrier. They are also what makes
# the container self-migrating on first boot.
COPY --from=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] /app/prisma ./prisma
COPY backend/package.json backend/package-lock.json ./

# 5000 = API, 4001 = mock carrier
EXPOSE 5000 4001

# Both the API and the outbox worker are started by src/index.ts.
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

```
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# DockSlot backend image.
#
# One image serves both long-running Node processes:
#   - the API + outbox worker:  node dist/index.js            (port 5000)
#   - the mock carrier service: node dist/mock-carrier/server.js (port 4001)
#
# The [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] is multi-stage so the Alpine toolchain needed to compile native
# modules (bcrypt) and the npm cache never reach the final image.
#
# Runtime dependencies are intentionally *not* pruned: docker-compose starts
# the container with `prisma db push` and `prisma db seed`, and the seed is
# invoked through ts-node, so the Prisma CLI, ts-node and TypeScript must be
# present at runtime.

FROM node:18-alpine AS [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
WORKDIR /app

# Prisma's query engine links against OpenSSL on Alpine. python3/make/g++ are
# only used if bcrypt has no musl pre[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] and compiles from source.
RUN apk add --no-cache openssl libc6-compat python3 make g++

# Install from the lockfile first so this layer is cached until dependencies change.
COPY backend/package.json backend/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY backend/tsconfig.json ./
COPY backend/prisma ./prisma
COPY backend/src ./src

# `prisma generate` is platform-specific: running it inside the Alpine [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
# stage produces the musl query engine that the runtime stage will load. The
# datasource URL is never connected during generate, so a placeholder is fine.
ENV DATABASE_URL="mysql://[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@localhost:3306/[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]"
RUN npx prisma generate

# Compile TypeScript (src -> dist). This also produces dist/mock-carrier/server.js.
RUN npm run [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

FROM node:18-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app

RUN apk add --no-cache openssl libc6-compat

ENV NODE_ENV=production

# Copy the dependency tree and compiled output from the [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] stage. Ownership
# is handed to the unprivileged `node` user: `prisma db push` regenerates the
# client into node_modules on first boot, and ts-node needs to read the project.
COPY --chown=node:node --from=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --chown=node:node --from=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] /app/dist ./dist
COPY --chown=node:node --from=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] /app/prisma ./prisma
COPY --chown=node:node backend/package.json backend/package-lock.json ./

USER node

# 5000 = API, 4001 = mock carrier
EXPOSE 5000 4001

# Starts the HTTP server and the transactional outbox worker (src/index.ts).
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]

```

```yaml
# DockSlot - full stack for local development / demos.
#
#   docker compose up --[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
#
# Services:
#   db            MySQL 8.0 with a persistent volume and a readiness healthcheck
#   mock-carrier  carrier webhook receiver (chaos off by default) on :4001
#   backend       runs `prisma db push` + `prisma db seed`, then the API and the
#                 transactional outbox worker on :5000
#
# Redis is intentionally not part of the stack: the app ships with an in-memory
# fallback (backend/src/config/redis.ts), so auth and rate limiting work in a
# single container without an extra dependency. Point REDIS_URL at a Redis
# instance later if you need state to survive restarts.
#
# Re-running `docker compose up` re-runs the seed. The seed is destructive by
# design (it clears and recreates the demo data), so `docker compose down -v`
# is the cleanest way to start over; use `docker compose restart backend` only
# when you want to keep existing bookings.
#
# Host port overrides (useful when something already listens on the defaults):
#   BACKEND_HOST_PORT=5050 MYSQL_HOST_PORT=3307 docker compose up --[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]

name: [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]

x-app: &app
  [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:
    context: .
    dockerfile: Dockerfile
  image: [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]-app:latest
  restart: unless-stopped

services:
  db:
    image: mysql:8.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_root}
      MYSQL_DATABASE: ${MYSQL_DATABASE:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_db}
      MYSQL_USER: ${MYSQL_USER:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]}
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_PASSWORD:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]}
    ports:
      # 3307 by default so a host MySQL on 3306 does not cause a port clash.
      - "${MYSQL_HOST_PORT:-3307}:3306"
    volumes:
      - mysql_data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      # CMD-SHELL so $$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD is expanded inside the container.
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - mysqladmin ping -h 127.0.0.1 -uroot -p"$$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" --silent
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30
      start_period: 30s

  mock-carrier:
    <<: *app
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      MOCK_CARRIER_PORT: "4001"
      # Deterministic success by default so end-to-end webhook tests are not
      # flaky. Set MOCK_CARRIER_SIMULATE_CHAOS=true to exercise retries/backoff.
      MOCK_CARRIER_SIMULATE_CHAOS: ${MOCK_CARRIER_SIMULATE_CHAOS:-false}
      MOCK_CARRIER_FAIL_RATE: ${MOCK_CARRIER_FAIL_RATE:-0.20}
      MOCK_CARRIER_HANG_RATE: ${MOCK_CARRIER_HANG_RATE:-0.05}
    ports:
      - "${MOCK_CARRIER_HOST_PORT:-4001}:4001"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - node
        - -e
        - "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:4001/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))"
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 10s

  backend:
    <<: *app
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      mock-carrier:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      PORT: "5000"
      # Prisma connection used by the app and by `prisma db push` / `db seed`.
      DATABASE_URL: mysql://${MYSQL_USER:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]}:${MYSQL_PASSWORD:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]}@db:3306/${MYSQL_DATABASE:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_db}
      # mysql2 pool configuration (backend/src/config/db.config.ts).
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "3306"
      DB_USER: ${MYSQL_USER:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]}
      DB_PASSWORD: ${MYSQL_PASSWORD:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]}
      DB_NAME: ${MYSQL_DATABASE:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]_db}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]-local-jwt-secret-change-me}
      JWT_EXPIRES_IN: ${JWT_EXPIRES_IN:-15m}
      JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN: ${JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN:-7d}
      APP_URL: http://localhost:${BACKEND_HOST_PORT:-5000}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: "3000"
      # Transactional outbox worker -> mock carrier inside the compose network.
      OUTBOX_WORKER_ENABLED: ${OUTBOX_WORKER_ENABLED:-true}
      CARRIER_NOTIFY_URL: http://mock-carrier:4001/notify
      OUTBOX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS: ${OUTBOX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS:-5000}
      OUTBOX_MAX_RETRIES: ${OUTBOX_MAX_RETRIES:-5}
    ports:
      - "${BACKEND_HOST_PORT:-5000}:5000"
    # `exec` makes node PID 1 so compose stop/restart reaches the app's SIGTERM
    # handler (graceful worker drain + Prisma disconnect).
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -e
        echo "[backend] Applying schema (prisma db push)..."
        npx prisma db push
        echo "[backend] Loading seed data (prisma db seed)..."
        npx prisma db seed
        echo "[backend] Starting API and outbox worker..."
        exec node dist/index.js
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - node
        - -e
        - "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:5000/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))"
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      # db push + seed can take a while on first boot.
      start_period: 90s

volumes:
  mysql_data:
    driver: local

```

```text
generator client {

}

}

  DOCK_MANAGER
  CARRIER_ADMIN
  DISPATCHER
}

enum DockStatus {
  ACTIVE
  MAINTENANCE
}

enum BookingStatus {
  BOOKED
  CANCELLED
  ARRIVED
  NO_SHOW
  COMPLETED
}

model Organization {
  id        Int              @id @default(autoincrement())
  name      String
  type      OrganizationType
  createdAt DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime         @updatedAt

  users       User[]
  warehouses  Warehouse[]
  bookings    Booking[]    @relation("CarrierBookings")
  invitations Invitation[]

  @@map("organizations")
}

  email                String    @unique

  lockUntil            DateTime?
  totpSecret           String?
  isTwoFactorEnabled   Boolean   @default(false)
  createdAt            DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt            DateTime  @updatedAt

  organization Organization @relation(fields: [organizationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  auditLogs    AuditLog[]

  @@index([organizationId])
  @@map("users")
}

model Warehouse {
  id                Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  organizationId    Int
  name              String
  address           String
  timezone          String
  slotLengthMinutes Int      @default(30)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())

  operatingHours OperatingHour[]

  @@index([organizationId])
  @@map("warehouses")
}

  updatedAt   DateTime   @updatedAt

  @@index([warehouseId])
  @@map("docks")
}
```

Implemented and verified the Docker stack end-to-end.

## Files created

- **`Dockerfile`** (root) — multi-stage `node:18-alpine`: dependency install + Prisma generate + `tsc` in a [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] stage (with `openssl`, `python3/make/g++` for bcrypt), then a slim runtime stage running as the unprivileged `node` user. Keeps dev dependencies available because the startup path needs the Prisma CLI and `ts-node` for the seed. Exposes `5000` (API) and `4001` (mock carrier).
- **`docker-compose.yml`** (root) — three services:
  - `db`: MySQL 8.0, named volume `mysql_data`, `mysqladmin ping` healthcheck.
  - `backend`: waits for `db` **and** `mock-carrier` health; runs `npx prisma db push` → `npx prisma db seed` → `exec node dist/index.js` (server + outbox worker in one process, with graceful SIGTERM). Healthcheck hits `GET /health`.
  - `mock-carrier`: runs `dist/mock-carrier/server.js` on port 4001, chaos simulation off by default for deterministic e2e.
- **`.dockerignore`** (root) — excludes `node_modules`, `dist`, `.env*`, `.git`, `frontend`, etc.

## Existing pieces left as-is

`backend/prisma/seed.ts` already seeds 4 organizations (2 carriers), 3 warehouses, 11 docks and 8 users — including `dispatcher@swiftfreight.com` / `[REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]word]`. `package.json` already contains `"prisma": { "seed": "ts-node prisma/seed.ts" }`. Its delete order is safe (`audit_logs`/`dock_closures` cascade from bookings/docks).

## One code change was required

`uuid@14` is ESM-only, so the CommonJS [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] crashed on the Node 18 image (`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM`) — it only worked locally because Node 22 supports `require(ESM)`. `backend/src/middleware/requestLogger.ts:4` now uses Node's built-in `crypto.randomUUID()` (same v4 UUID, no dependency, Node 18-safe).

## Verified live

Brought the stack up on alternate host ports (this machine already uses 5000/4001/3306), and confirmed:

- all three containers reached **healthy**; `GET /health` → `200 {"status":"UP","database":"connected"}`;
- seed loaded 4 orgs / 8 users / 3 warehouses / 11 docks, and login with the seeded dispatcher succeeded;
- `POST /api/bookings` → `201`, outbox row `COMPLETED`, and the mock carrier received `BOOKING_CREATED` with the same `requestId` (`e2e-compose-booking-1`) echoed through the HTTP response, DB payload, and webhook body;
- `docker compose restart backend` on an existing volume re-runs `db push`/seed and returns healthy.

Test containers and volume were removed afterward.

## Usage notes

- Start with `docker compose up --[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]`; API at `http://localhost:5000`, mock carrier at `http://localhost:4001`.
- **MySQL is published on 3307** by default so a host MySQL on 3306 doesn't collide. Override any host port: `BACKEND_HOST_PORT=5050 MYSQL_HOST_PORT=3307 docker compose up --[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]`.
- **Redis is intentionally not a service**: `backend/src/config/redis.ts` falls back to an in-memory store, so auth/rate limiting work in a single container. Add a Redis service and `REDIS_URL` later if you need that state to survive restarts.
- The seed is destructive by design, so every `docker compose up` resets demo data (documented in the compose header).

```text
/**
 * Retrieves available time slots for a warehouse on a given date.
 * GET /api/warehouses/:warehouseId/slots?date=YYYY-MM-DD
 */
export const getAvailableSlots = async (req: Request, res: Response): Promise<void> => {
  try {
    const rawId = req.params.warehouseId;
    const warehouseId = parseParamId(rawId);
    if (isNaN(warehouseId)) {
      res.status(400).json({
        success: false,
        message: 'Invalid warehouse ID.',
      });
      return;
    }

    const dateQuery = (req.query.date || req.query.targetDate) as string;
    if (!dateQuery || typeof dateQuery !== 'string' || !dateQuery.trim()) {
      res.status(400).json({
        success: false,
        message: 'Missing required query parameter: date (expected format: YYYY-MM-DD).',
      });
      return;
    }

    const trimmedDate = dateQuery.trim();
    if (!isValidDateString(trimmedDate)) {
      res.status(400).json({
        success: false,
        message: 'Invalid date format. Expected a valid calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format.',
      });
      return;
    }

    const slots = await warehouseService.getAvailableSlots(warehouseId, trimmedDate);
    res.status(200).json({
      success: true,
      data: slots,
    });
  } catch (error: any) {
    const status = error.status || 500;
    res.status(status).json({
      success: false,
      message: error.message || 'Internal server error while fetching available slots.',
    });
  }
};
```

```text
   * Updates warehouse settings (e.g., default slotLengthMinutes) with strict tenant isolation.
   * Validates that slotLengthMinutes is a valid increment (e.g., 30, 45, 60 minutes) that divides evenly
   * into operating schedules, and updates both the warehouse and its operating hours records.
   * Existing confirmed bookings retain their original time ranges and remain unaffected.
   */
  async updateWarehouseSettings(
    warehouseId: number,
    organizationId: number,
    data: UpdateWarehouseSettingsInput
  ) {
    if (!warehouseId || isNaN(warehouseId)) {
      throw { status: 400, message: 'Invalid warehouse ID.' };
    }

    const warehouse = await prisma.warehouse.findUnique({
      where: { id: warehouseId },
      include: {
        operatingHours: true,
        docks: true,
      },
    });

    if (!warehouse) {
      throw { status: 404, message: 'Warehouse not found.' };
    }

    if (warehouse.organizationId !== organizationId) {
      throw {
        status: 403,
        message: 'Forbidden. You do not have permission to manage settings for this warehouse.',
      };
    }

    if (data.slotLengthMinutes !== undefined) {
      const slotLength = data.slotLengthMinutes;
      const allowedIncrements = [15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120];

      if (
        typeof slotLength !== 'number' ||
        !Number.isInteger(slotLength) ||
        slotLength <= 0 ||
        (!allowedIncrements.includes(slotLength) && 1440 % slotLength !== 0)
      ) {
        throw {
          status: 400,
          message: `Invalid slotLengthMinutes: ${slotLength}. Allowed increments must divide evenly into operating schedules (e.g., 30, 45, 60 minutes).`,
        };
      }
    }

    if (data.timezone) {
      const trimmedTz = data.timezone.trim();
      if (!isValidIanaTimeZone(trimmedTz)) {
        throw { status: 400, message: `Invalid IANA timezone string: '${trimmedTz}'.` };
      }
    }

    const isNameChanging = data.name !== undefined && data.name.trim() !== warehouse.name;
    const isAddressChanging = data.address !== undefined && data.address.trim() !== warehouse.address;
    const isTimezoneChanging = data.timezone !== undefined && data.timezone.trim() !== warehouse.timezone;
    const isCoreInfoChanging = isNameChanging || isAddressChanging || isTimezoneChanging;

    if (isCoreInfoChanging) {
      const activeBookedCount = await prisma.booking.count({
        where: {
          dock: {
            warehouseId,
          },
          status: BookingStatus.BOOKED,
        },
      });

      if (activeBookedCount > 0) {
        throw {
          status: 400,
          message: `Cannot update warehouse name, address, or timezone while there are active bookings with status 'BOOKED'.`,
        };
      }
    }

    const result = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
      const updated = await tx.warehouse.update({
        where: { id: warehouseId },
        data: {
          ...(data.name && { name: data.name.trim() }),
          ...(data.address && { address: data.address.trim() }),
          ...(data.timezone && { timezone: data.timezone.trim() }),
          ...(data.slotLengthMinutes !== undefined && { slotLengthMinutes: data.slotLengthMinutes }),
        },
        include: {
          docks: true,
          operatingHours: true,
        },
      });

      if (data.slotLengthMinutes !== undefined) {
        await tx.operatingHour.updateMany({
          where: { warehouseId },
          data: {
            slotLengthMinutes: data.slotLengthMinutes,
          },
        });
      }

      return updated;
    });

    return result;
  }
```

```text
+import { fromZonedTime, toZonedTime, formatInTimeZone } from 'date-fns-tz';
+
+/**
+ * Validates whether a given string is a valid IANA time zone identifier.
+ */
+export function isValidIanaTimeZone(timeZone: string): boolean {
+  if (!timeZone || typeof timeZone !== 'string' || timeZone.trim() === '') {
+    return false;
+  }
+  try {
+    Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { timeZone: timeZone.trim() });
+    return true;
+  } catch {
+    return false;
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Validates whether a date string is in valid YYYY-MM-DD calendar format.
+ */
+export function isValidDateString(dateStr: string): boolean {
+  if (!dateStr || typeof dateStr !== 'string') return false;
+  if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(dateStr)) return false;
+
+  const [yearStr, monthStr, dayStr] = dateStr.split('-');
+  const year = parseInt(yearStr, 10);
+  const month = parseInt(monthStr, 10);
+  const day = parseInt(dayStr, 10);
+
+  if (month < 1 || month > 12 || day < 1 || day > 31) return false;
+
+  const dateObj = new Date(year, month - 1, day);
+  return (
+    dateObj.getFullYear() === year &&
+    dateObj.getMonth() === month - 1 &&
+    dateObj.getDate() === day
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * Determines the day of the week (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, ..., 6 = Saturday)
+ * for a specific calendar date in the warehouse's IANA timezone.
+ */
+export function getDayOfWeekInTimeZone(dateStr: string, timeZone: string): number {
+  // Use noon (12:00:00) in the given timezone to avoid midnight DST transitions
+  const localNoon = fromZonedTime(`${dateStr} 12:00:00`, timeZone);
+  const zonedDate = toZonedTime(localNoon, timeZone);
+  return zonedDate.getDay();
+}
+
+/**
+ * Parses "HH:mm" time string into total minutes from start of day.
+ */
+export function timeStringToMinutes(timeStr: string): number {
+  const [hours, minutes] = timeStr.split(':').map((part) => parseInt(part, 10));
+  return hours * 60 + minutes;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Converts total minutes from start of day into "HH:mm" string.
+ */
+export function minutesToTimeString(totalMinutes: number): string {
+  const hours = Math.floor(totalMinutes / 60);
+  const minutes = totalMinutes % 60;
+  return `${String(hours).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(minutes).padStart(2, '0')}`;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Generates all discrete time slot intervals [start, end] between openTime and closeTime
+ * for a given slot length in minutes.
+ * E.g., openTime: "08:00", closeTime: "10:00", slotLengthMinutes: 30
+ * returns: [{ start: "08:00", end: "08:30" }, { start: "08:30", end: "09:00" }, ...]
+ */
+export function generateTimeIntervals(
+  openTime: string,
+  closeTime: string,
+  slotLengthMinutes: number
+): Array<{ start: string; end: string }> {
+  if (slotLengthMinutes <= 0) return [];
+
+  let currentStartMin = timeStringToMinutes(openTime);
+  const closeMin = timeStringToMinutes(closeTime);
+  const intervals: Array<{ start: string; end: string }> = [];
+
+  while (currentStartMin + slotLengthMinutes <= closeMin) {
+    const currentEndMin = currentStartMin + slotLengthMinutes;
+    intervals.push({
+      start: minutesToTimeString(currentStartMin),
+      end: minutesToTimeString(currentEndMin),
+    });
+    currentStartMin = currentEndMin;
+  }
+
+  return intervals;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Converts a localized calendar date and "HH:mm" time in a given IANA timezone into a UTC Date object.
+ */
+export function zonedDateAndTimeToUtc(dateStr: string, timeStr: string, timeZone: string): Date {
+  const normalizedTime = timeStr.length === 5 ? `${timeStr}:00` : timeStr;
+  return fromZonedTime(`${dateStr} ${normalizedTime}`, timeZone);
+}
```

```text
21	export function isValidDateString(dateStr: string): boolean {
22	  if (!dateStr || typeof dateStr !== 'string') return false;
23	  if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(dateStr)) return false;
24	
25	  const [yearStr, monthStr, dayStr] = dateStr.split('-');

31
```

```typescript
import { prisma } from './src/config/db.config';
import { warehouseService } from './src/services/warehouse.service';

const toMin = (s: string) => {
  const [h, m] = s.split(':').map(Number);
  return h * 60 + m;
};

const DAY_MAP: Record<string, number> = { Sun: 7, Mon: 1, Tue: 2, Wed: 3, Thu: 4, Fri: 5, Sat: 6 };

async function main() {
  const ws = await prisma.warehouse.findMany({
    include: {
      operatingHours: true,
      docks: {
        include: {
          closures: { where: { startTime: { lte: new Date() }, endTime: { gte: new Date() } } },
        },
      },
    },
  });
  const dates = ['2026-10-19', '2026-10-24', '2026-10-25'];
  let anomalies = 0;
  let checked = 0;
  let skipped = 0;

  for (const w of ws) {
    for (const ds of dates) {
      const u = new Date(ds + 'T00:00:00Z');
      const dow = DAY_MAP[new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: w.timezone, weekday: 'short' }).format(u)];
      const hour =
        w.operatingHours.find((h) => h.dayOfWeek === dow) ||
        (dow === 7 ? w.operatingHours.find((h) => h.dayOfWeek === 0) : undefined);
      if (!hour) {
        skipped++;
        continue;
      }
      const open = toMin(hour.openTime);
      const close = hour.closeTime === '24:00' ? 1440 : toMin(hour.closeTime);
      const expected = Math.max(0, Math.floor((close - open) / hour.slotLengthMinutes));
      const groups = await warehouseService.getAvailableSlots(w.id, ds);
      checked++;
      for (const g of groups) {
        if (g.slots.length !== expected) {
          const bookings = await prisma.booking.count({
            where: { dockId: g.dockId, status: { in: ['BOOKED', 'ARRIVED'] } },
          });
          console.log(
            'MISMATCH wh', w.id, w.name, 'tz', w.timezone, 'date', ds, 'dock', g.dockId,
            'got', g.slots.length, 'expected', expected, 'bookings', bookings,
            'hours', `${hour.openTime}-${hour.closeTime}/${hour.slotLengthMinutes}`
          );
          anomalies++;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  console.log('checked', checked, 'skipped(closed)', skipped, 'anomalies', anomalies);
  await prisma.$disconnect();
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e);
  process.exit(1);
});

```

```ts
/**
 * Resolves open/close times into a minute range, interpreting a close time at or
 * before the open time as the end of the following day. This covers:
 *   - "24:00" (1440)
 *   - midnight close "00:00" (e.g. 08:00-00:00 -> 08:00-24:00)
 *   - overnight windows (e.g. 22:00-06:00 -> 22:00-30:00)
 */
export function resolveOperatingWindowMinutes(openTime, closeTime): { openMin, closeMin } {
  const openMin = timeStringToMinutes(openTime);
  let closeMin = timeStringToMinutes(closeTime);
  if (closeMin <= openMin) {
    closeMin += 1440;
  }
  return { openMin, closeMin };
}
```

```ts
export function generateTimeIntervals(openTime, closeTime, slotLengthMinutes) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(slotLengthMinutes) || slotLengthMinutes <= 0) return [];
  const { openMin, closeMin } = resolveOperatingWindowMinutes(openTime, closeTime);
  const intervals = [];
  let currentStartMin = openMin;
  while (currentStartMin + slotLengthMinutes <= closeMin) {
    const currentEndMin = currentStartMin + slotLengthMinutes;
    intervals.push({ start: minutesToTimeString(currentStartMin), end: minutesToTimeString(currentEndMin) });
    currentStartMin = currentEndMin;
  }
  return intervals;
}
```

`zonedDateAndTimeToUtc` must handle hours ≥ 24:

```ts
export function zonedDateAndTimeToUtc(dateStr, timeStr, timeZone) {
  const [hoursStr, minutesStr = '00'] = timeStr.split(':');
  const hours = parseInt(hoursStr, 10);
  const minutes = parseInt(minutesStr, 10);
  const dayOffset = Math.floor(hours / 24);
  const localHours = ((hours % 24) + 24) % 24;
  const [year, month, day] = dateStr.split('-').map(Number);
  const target = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day + dayOffset));
  const targetStr = target.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const normalizedTime = `${String(localHours).padStart(2,'0')}:${String(minutes).padStart(2,'0')}:00`;
  return fromZonedTime(`${targetStr} ${normalizedTime}`, timeZone);
}
```

This subsumes the old hours===24 branch (dayOffset=1, localHours=0) exactly.

```ts
/**
 * Resolves an operating window into minutes from midnight.
 * closeTime values at or before openTime roll over to the following day:
 *   - "00:00" close means midnight at the end of the day (08:00-00:00 -> 08:00-24:00)
 *   - overnight windows (22:00-06:00 -> 22:00-30:00) are supported
 *   - "24:00" is already 1440
 */
export function resolveOperatingWindowMinutes(openTime: string, closeTime: string): { openMin: number; closeMin: number } {
  const openMin = timeStringToMinutes(openTime);
  let closeMin = timeStringToMinutes(closeTime);
  if (closeMin <= openMin) {
    closeMin += 1440;
  }
  return { openMin, closeMin };
}
```

```ts
const formatSlotClock = useCallback((timeStr?: string): string | null => {
  if (!timeStr) return null;
  const [hStr, mStr = "0"] = timeStr.split(":");
  const total = Number(hStr) * 60 + Number(mStr);
  if (!Number.isFinite(total)) return null;
  const normalized = ((total % 1440) + 1440) % 1440;
  const h = Math.floor(normalized / 60);
  const m = normalized % 60;
  const period = h >= 12 ? "PM" : "AM";
  const h12 = h % 12 === 0 ? 12 : h % 12;
  return `${h12}:${String(m).padStart(2, "0")} ${period}`;
}, []);
```

```ts
  return `${formatDateTime(slot.slotStartTime, "h:mm a")} - ${formatDateTime(slot.slotEndTime, "h:mm a")}`;
}, [formatSlotClock]);
```

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  generateTimeIntervals,
  resolveOperatingWindowMinutes,
  normalizeTimeOfDay,
  zonedDateAndTimeToUtc,
  timeStringToMinutes,
} from '../src/utils/time.utils';

describe('generateTimeIntervals', () => {
  it('generates the full day for a standard weekday window', () => {
    const intervals = generateTimeIntervals('08:00', '18:00', 30);

    expect(intervals).toHaveLength(20);
    expect(intervals[0]).toEqual({ start: '08:00', end: '08:30' });
    expect(intervals[intervals.length - 1]).toEqual({ start: '17:30', end: '18:00' });
  });

  it('generates the short Saturday window', () => {
    expect(generateTimeIntervals('08:00', '13:00', 30)).toHaveLength(10);
  });

  it('generates 45-minute slots across a 12-hour window', () => {
    const intervals = generateTimeIntervals('07:00', '19:00', 45);

    expect(intervals).toHaveLength(16);
    expect(intervals[intervals.length - 1]).toEqual({ start: '18:15', end: '19:00' });
  });

  it('drops a trailing partial interval when the window is not evenly divisible', () => {
    const intervals = generateTimeIntervals('08:00', '18:00', 45);

    expect(intervals).toHaveLength(13);
    expect(intervals[intervals.length - 1]).toEqual({ start: '17:15', end: '18:00' });
  });

  it('generates a full 24 hours for 00:00-24:00', () => {
    const intervals = generateTimeIntervals('00:00', '24:00', 45);

    expect(intervals).toHaveLength(32);
    expect(intervals[intervals.length - 1]).toEqual({ start: '23:15', end: '24:00' });
  });

  it('treats 00:00-00:00 as a 24/7 window', () => {
    expect(generateTimeIntervals('00:00', '00:00', 30)).toHaveLength(48);
  });

  it('treats a midnight close as the end of the day', () => {
    const intervals = generateTimeIntervals('08:00', '00:00', 30);

    expect(intervals).toHaveLength(32);
    expect(intervals[intervals.length - 1]).toEqual({ start: '23:30', end: '24:00' });
  });

  it('supports overnight windows that roll past midnight', () => {
    const intervals = generateTimeIntervals('22:00', '06:00', 60);

    expect(intervals).toHaveLength(8);
    expect(intervals[0]).toEqual({ start: '22:00', end: '23:00' });
    expect(intervals[intervals.length - 1]).toEqual({ start: '05:00', end: '06:00' });
  });

  it('returns no intervals for non-positive slot lengths', () => {
    expect(generateTimeIntervals('08:00', '18:00', 0)).toEqual([]);
    expect(generateTimeIntervals('08:00', '18:00', -30)).toEqual([]);
    expect(generateTimeIntervals('08:00', '18:00', Number.NaN)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('resolveOperatingWindowMinutes', () => {
  it('keeps regular daytime windows unchanged', () => {
    expect(resolveOperatingWindowMinutes('08:00', '18:00')).toEqual({
      openMin: 480,
      closeMin: 1080,
    });
  });

  it('keeps 24:00 as 1440', () => {
    expect(resolveOperatingWindowMinutes('00:00', '24:00')).toEqual({
      openMin: 0,
      closeMin: 1440,
    });
  });

  it('rolls a midnight close to the end of the day', () => {
    expect(resolveOperatingWindowMinutes('08:00', '00:00')).toEqual({
      openMin: 480,
      closeMin: 1440,
    });
  });

  it('rolls overnight closes into the following day', () => {
    expect(resolveOperatingWindowMinutes('22:00', '06:00')).toEqual({
      openMin: 1320,
      closeMin: 1800,
    });
  });
});

describe('normalizeTimeOfDay', () => {
  it('wraps rolled-over boundaries back into 00:00-23:59', () => {
    expect(normalizeTimeOfDay('24:00')).toBe('00:00');
    expect(normalizeTimeOfDay('25:30')).toBe('01:30');
    expect(normalizeTimeOfDay('30:00')).toBe('06:00');
    expect(normalizeTimeOfDay('08:30')).toBe('08:30');
  });
});

describe('zonedDateAndTimeToUtc', () => {
  it('resolves a regular local time to UTC', () => {
    // Asia/Colombo is UTC+5:30 with no daylight saving.
    const utc = zonedDateAndTimeToUtc('2026-10-19', '08:00', 'Asia/Colombo');

    expect(utc.toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-19T02:30:00.000Z');
  });

  it('resolves 24:00 to midnight on the following day', () => {
    const utc = zonedDateAndTimeToUtc('2026-10-19', '24:00', 'Asia/Colombo');

    expect(utc.toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-19T18:30:00.000Z');
  });

  it('resolves boundaries past midnight for overnight windows', () => {
    const utc = zonedDateAndTimeToUtc('2026-10-19', '25:30', 'Asia/Colombo');

    expect(utc.toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-19T20:00:00.000Z');
  });
});

describe('timeStringToMinutes', () => {
  it('parses HH:mm and 24:00', () => {
    expect(timeStringToMinutes('00:00')).toBe(0);
    expect(timeStringToMinutes('08:30')).toBe(510);
    expect(timeStringToMinutes('24:00')).toBe(1440);
  });
});

```

```tsx
// Renders a warehouse-local "HH:mm" boundary (including rolled-over overnight
// values like "25:30") as a 12-hour clock label, e.g. "8:00 AM".
const formatSlotClock = useCallback((timeStr?: string): string | null => {
  if (!timeStr) return null;
  const [hoursStr, minutesStr = "0"] = timeStr.split(":");
  const hours = Number(hoursStr);
  const minutes = Number(minutesStr);
  if (!Number.isFinite(hours) || !Number.isFinite(minutes)) return null;
  const totalMinutes = ((hours * 60 + minutes) % 1440 + 1440) % 1440;
  const normalizedHours = Math.floor(totalMinutes / 60);
  const normalizedMinutes = totalMinutes % 60;
  const period = normalizedHours >= 12 ? "PM" : "AM";
  const twelveHour = normalizedHours % 12 === 0 ? 12 : normalizedHours % 12;
  return `${twelveHour}:${String(normalizedMinutes).padStart(2, "0")} ${period}`;
}, []);

// Slots are generated in the warehouse's own time zone; prefer the local
// start/end returned by the API so a dispatcher abroad sees the dock's clock.
const formatSlotWindow = useCallback(
  (slot: { slotStartTime: string; slotEndTime: string; localStartTime?: string; localEndTime?: string }): string => {
    const localStart = formatSlotClock(slot.localStartTime);
    const localEnd = formatSlotClock(slot.localEndTime);
    if (localStart && localEnd) return `${localStart} - ${localEnd}`;
    return `${formatDateTime(slot.slotStartTime, "h:mm a")} - ${formatDateTime(slot.slotEndTime, "h:mm a")}`;
  },
  [formatSlotClock],
);
```

```typescript
import { PrismaClient, DockStatus } from '@prisma/client';
import { warehouseService } from './src/services/warehouse.service';

const prisma = new PrismaClient();
const DAYS = [2, 3]; // Tue/Wed only

async function main() {
  const org = await prisma.organization.create({
    data: { name: `Overnight Audit ${Date.now()}`, type: 'WAREHOUSE_OPERATOR' },
  });

  const warehouse = await prisma.warehouse.create({
    data: {
      organizationId: org.id,
      name: 'Overnight Audit WH',
      address: 'tmp',
      timezone: 'Asia/Colombo',
      docks: { create: [{ name: 'Night Bay', status: DockStatus.ACTIVE }] },
      operatingHours: {
        create: DAYS.map((dayOfWeek) => ({
          dayOfWeek,
          openTime: '22:00',
          closeTime: '06:00',
          slotLengthMinutes: 60,
        })),
      },
    },
  });

  try {
    // 2026-10-20 is a Tuesday in Colombo.
    const slots = await warehouseService.getAvailableSlots(warehouse.id, '2026-10-20');
    const free = slots[0]?.slots ?? [];
    console.log('overnight slots:', free.length);
    console.log('first:', free[0]);
    console.log('last:', free[free.length - 1]);
    console.log(
      'UTC instants ordered:',
      free.every((s, i) => i === 0 || new Date(s.slotStartTime) > new Date(free[i - 1].slotStartTime))
    );

    // Midnight-close schedule: 20:00 -> 00:00, 30 min = 8 slots.
    await prisma.operatingHour.updateMany({
      where: { warehouseId: warehouse.id },
      data: { openTime: '20:00', closeTime: '00:00', slotLengthMinutes: 30 },
    });
    const midnightSlots = (await warehouseService.getAvailableSlots(warehouse.id, '2026-10-20'))[0].slots;
    console.log('midnight-close slots:', midnightSlots.length, 'first', midnightSlots[0]?.localStartTime, 'last', midnightSlots[midnightSlots.length - 1]?.localStartTime, '-', midnightSlots[midnightSlots.length - 1]?.localEndTime);
  } finally {
    await prisma.operatingHour.deleteMany({ where: { warehouseId: warehouse.id } });
    await prisma.dock.deleteMany({ where: { warehouseId: warehouse.id } });
    await prisma.warehouse.delete({ where: { id: warehouse.id } });
    await prisma.organization.delete({ where: { id: org.id } });
    await prisma.$disconnect();
  }
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e);
  process.exit(1);
});

```

     ```ts
       openTime: string,
       closeTime: string
     ): { openMin: number; closeMin: number } {
       const openMin = timeStringToMinutes(openTime);
       let closeMin = timeStringToMinutes(closeTime);
       if (closeMin <= openMin) {
         closeMin += 1440;
       }
       return { openMin, closeMin };
     }

     export function generateTimeIntervals(
       openTime: string,
       closeTime: string,
       slotLengthMinutes: number
     ): Array<{ start: string; end: string }> {
       if (!Number.isFinite(slotLengthMinutes) || slotLengthMinutes <= 0) return [];
       const { openMin, closeMin } = resolveOperatingWindowMinutes(openTime, closeTime);
       const intervals: Array<{ start: string; end: string }> = [];
       let currentStartMin = openMin;
       while (currentStartMin + slotLengthMinutes <= closeMin) {
         const currentEndMin = currentStartMin + slotLengthMinutes;
         intervals.push({ start: minutesToTimeString(currentStartMin), end: minutesToTimeString(currentEndMin) });
         currentStartMin = currentEndMin;
       }
       return intervals;
     }

     export function normalizeTimeOfDay(timeStr: string): string {
       const totalMinutes = timeStringToMinutes(timeStr);
       const minutesInDay = ((totalMinutes % 1440) + 1440) % 1440;
       return minutesToTimeString(minutesInDay);
     }

     export function zonedDateAndTimeToUtc(dateStr: string, timeStr: string, timeZone: string): Date {
       const [hoursStr, minutesStr = '00'] = timeStr.split(':');
       const hours = parseInt(hoursStr, 10);
       const minutes = parseInt(minutesStr, 10);
       const dayOffset = Math.floor(hours / 24);
       const hoursInDay = ((hours % 24) + 24) % 24;
       let targetDateStr = dateStr;
       if (dayOffset !== 0) {
         const [year, month, day] = dateStr.split('-').map(Number);
         const targetDate = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day + dayOffset));
         targetDateStr = targetDate.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
       }
       const normalizedTime = `${String(hoursInDay).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(minutes).padStart(2, '0')}:00`;
       return fromZonedTime(`${targetDateStr} ${normalizedTime}`, timeZone);
     }
     ```
     Why important: fixes the reported/generator bug where `08:00–00:00` (midnight close) or overnight windows (`22:00–06:00`) produced **zero** slots.

_**Agent (deepseek-v4-flash 2026-10-17 12:04:27Z)**_

Reviewed the full slot-generation flow end to end. Here's what I found and changed.

## Is the math [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]? No — with one important exception

I audited the generator against every row in the DB: **1070 warehouse/date combinations, 0 anomalies** versus `floor((closeMin - openMin) / slotLengthMinutes)`. Live HTTP spot-checks matched too (Colombo 20 slots/dock on weekdays, 10 on Saturday; Jebel Ali 16/dock Sun–Thu, 8 on Saturday). So for seeded warehouse data, the counts were already correct — **except** for the cases below, which returned **zero**.

## Real defects found and fixed

**1. `generateTimeIntervals` returned 0 intervals for midnight-close and overnight shifts** (`backend/src/utils/time.utils.ts`)

The old loop compared `close <= open` and bailed. Any schedule like `08:00–00:00` (close at midnight) or `22:00–06:00` (overnight) produced an empty list, hence "no slots". New `resolveOperatingWindowMinutes()` adds 1440 to a close time that is `<=` open, and the loop now counts from `openMin` to `closeMin` (which may exceed 1440), emitting `"23:30"/"24:00"` or `"29:00"/"30:00"` style bounds.

- `00:00–00:00` → 48 slots (24/7)
- `08:00–00:00` @30 → 32 slots, last `23:30–24:00`
- `22:00–06:00` @60 → 8 slots, last raw `29:00–30:00` → normalized `05:00–06:00`

**2. `zonedDateAndTimeToUtc` couldn't resolve times past 24:00.** Generalized to accept `hours >= 24`, rolling the date forward by the day offset before calling `fromZonedTime`. `normalizeTimeOfDay()` (new) wraps any such value back to `HH:mm` for display.

**3. The same broken window logic was duplicated in booking validation** (`booking.service.ts`). `validateSlotOperatingHours` now uses `resolveOperatingWindowMinutes`, accepts the after-midnight tail of the *previous* day's overnight shift, and normalizes `startMin`/`endMin` before comparing against the window — so overnight slots are now bookable, not just generatable.

**4. `getAvailableSlots` under-fetched bookings/closures for overnight windows** (`warehouse.service.ts`). The lookup window was capped at local `endOfDayUtc`; it's now widened to the last generated interval's end, so a `22:00–06:00` schedule doesn't show slots that are actually already booked.

**5. The `dockId` query param was documented but silently ignored.** Implemented server-side (`warehouse.controller.ts` + `getAvailableSlots(warehouseId, date, dockId?)`), 400 on invalid values, and documented in `open-api.json`.

**6. The Dispatcher rendered slot windows in the *browser's* timezone.** The API returns `localStartTime`/`localEndTime` in warehouse-local time, but `DispatcherDashboard.tsx` ran the UTC instants through `formatDateTime`. That means a 20-slot day could *look* like fewer slots when times collided/wrapped across midnight in the browser locale. Now uses `formatSlotWindow()` (which prefers the local fields, wraps `24:00` back to `12:00 AM`), plus a `Times in <timezone> · tap a window to book` header note and a `slotDate · window (timezone)` line in the booking modal. Also pinned the results header to the date that was actually searched (`searchedDate`), so changing the date input can't relabel stale results.

## Likely cause of what you were seeing

Searching **today** filters out slots whose start has already [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed — that's by design and is the most common reason a day looks under-populated. The empty state now says so explicitly.

The only way to get a genuine **zero** for a warehouse created through the UI: `WarehouseAdminDashboard`'s weekly-schedule editor doesn't persist (`handleSaveScheduleDesign` only toasts), and there is no operating-hours CRUD endpoint at all. A warehouse created via the UI has no operating-hour rows, so it has no slots. I left that alone — it's a missing feature, not a generator bug — but flagging it as the next thing to fix if you want UI-created warehouses to work.
